properties.name: MEASURED: reading ${PIPESTATUS[0]} one command late reports 0 for a run that exited 7 — a false GREEN produced by a cosmetic separator, twice in one session
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-29, after reporting a passing test suite that had actually FAILED.

═══ THE DEMONSTRATION, run both ways ═══

```text
bash -c 'exit 7' 2>&1 | tail -1
echo "--------"                      <- a cosmetic separator
echo ${PIPESTATUS[0]}   ->  0       <- WRONG, and it reads as a pass

bash -c 'exit 7' 2>&1 | tail -1
echo ${PIPESTATUS[0]}   ->  7       <- correct
```

`PIPESTATUS` describes THE MOST RECENT PIPELINE, so any intervening command — `echo` included — overwrites it with that command's status, which is almost always 0. The separator that makes output readable is the thing that destroys the evidence.

═══ HOW IT ACTUALLY PRESENTED ═══

TWICE in one session, both times as a confident green:
1. `cargo test` printed `test result: FAILED. 7 passed; 1 failed` AND the line under it read `CARGO TEST EXIT=0`. The suite genuinely had a failing test; the exit code shown was the separator's.
2. `<binary> --import <doc> | tail -12` reported `IMPORT EXIT=0` while the import had exited 1 and written nothing. Here the fault is the sibling one — bare `$?` after a pipeline is the LAST element's status, so it measured `tail`.

⭐ BOTH ARE THE SAME FAMILY: the status read did not belong to the command being judged. And both are silent — the wrong number is a plausible number, in the right place, in the right format.

═══ 🛑 THE CAUSE I FIRST RECORDED WAS WRONG, WHICH IS THE SECOND FINDING ═══

The first diagnosis written down was *"`systemd-run --user --scope` does not propagate exit codes"*. It is FALSE and was refuted by one measurement: `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=1G bash -c 'exit 7'` returns 7, identically to running it bare. The wrapper was innocent and was blamed because it was the unfamiliar element in the line — the plausible suspect rather than the measured one. It had already been written into a handoff note before the check was run, and would have taught the next session to distrust the wrong thing.

═══ WHAT TO DO INSTEAD ═══

Read the status in the SAME command as the thing that produced it, and prefer having the runner say so itself:

```text
systemd-run --user --scope ... bash -c 'cargo test ...; echo "INNER_EXIT=$?"'
```

⚠️ WHY THIS IS WORTH A NODE IN A DESIGN GRAPH: `rule:a-green-gate-is-the-weakest-evidence` is the project's standing stance, and this is a mechanism that FABRICATES one from a run that failed. The reflow2 gate list in AGENTS.md is run by hand by agents, and an agent that reports the list green on this idiom has told the user something false about every gate at once.

⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any committed script or workflow in this repo reads a pipeline status late. Grepped for `systemd-run` in AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .github/workflows and tools/ — one hit, in AGENTS.md prose, and it is not a gate. CI itself uses plain `run:` steps, so the hazard measured here is the AGENT'S shell, not the committed pipeline.
